results.corrected_extracted: The authors note that the forensic-pathology literature almost exclusively uses 'excited delirium' and describes only deaths, while the clinical literature uses both terms for the same presentation and includes survivors as well as deaths, and that deaths are more likely to be published and better documented (toxicology, police reports, witnesses); the first reader's appraisal is that this split ties the label, death and the recording of restraint together through the type of source, which the analysis (univariate tests only) did not stratify or adjust for.
